whyEn: The opening chapter supplies the vocabulary the whole exam is written in: what a paramedic system is made of, who regulates whom, and what 'professional' actually obligates you to do. The written paper likes four things from here — the handful of genuinely distinctive history milestones (not trivia for its own sake, but the ones that explain why EMS looks the way it does), the licensure/certification/registration distinctions, the online versus offline faces of medical direction with standing orders and protocols, and the roles-and-responsibilities sequence of a call from preparation to return to service. It is a low-weight chapter, but its definitions get reused silently inside questions from every other chapter.
whyZh: 开卷第一章提供的是整张考卷的『底层词汇表』：一个救护系统由什么组成、谁监管谁、『专业』二字究竟捆绑了哪些义务。笔试爱从这里出四类题——真正有辨识度的历史里程碑（不是为怀旧，而是解释今天的 EMS 为什么长这样）、执照/认证/注册三个词的区分、医疗指导的在线与离线两副面孔（含 standing orders 与 protocol 的关系），以及一次出勤从备勤到恢复待命的职责顺序。权重不高，但它的定义会悄悄嵌进其他所有章节的题干里。

points.en: The original responder job was 'scoop and swoop' — spot the sick or injured person, load, and race to a facility. Community expectations and research findings dismantled that model: today's paramedic handles everything from life threats to simply listening, and the public grades you against what television and news coverage taught them to expect.
points.zh: 早期急救员的工作模式叫『scoop and swoop』——认出伤病员、抬上车、火速送院了事。社区期望和研究证据一起终结了这个模式：今天的救护员既要处理致命急症，也要给只需要倾诉的人当听众，而公众会拿电视和新闻报道塑造的形象来给你打分。

points.en: Certification or licensure grants the privilege — not the right — to treat a person who may be living one of the worst moments of their life. The price of that privilege is stated in the same breath: maintain your certification and continually upgrade knowledge and skills, because paramedicine is lifelong learning.
points.zh: 认证或执照给你的只是『特权』而非『权利』——去救治一个也许正处于人生最糟糕时刻的人。这份特权的代价在同一句话里写明：维持认证、持续更新知识与技能，因为救护这一行是终身学习的职业。

sections.titleEn: The History of Paramedicine: Milestones That Get Tested
sections.titleZh: 急救医学发展史：真正会被考的里程碑

points.en: Oldest datable root: around 1700 BCE in Babylon, care providers travelled to the patient's home, and the Code of Hammurabi — written by the king who invented rule by law — laid down protocols and payment for medical care, including punishment for malpractice. Provider-goes-to-patient stayed the default model until Napoleon's era.
points.zh: 可考的最早源头：约公元前1700年的巴比伦，医者上门到患者家中行医，而『以法治国』的汉谟拉比王颁布的《汉谟拉比法典》已经写明了医疗的操作规程与酬金——连治坏了怎么罚都有条款。『医生去找患者』这个模式一直沿用到拿破仑时代。

points.en: 1790s: physician Jean Larrey created the ambulances volantes — 'flying ambulances' — pushing care out to wounded soldiers in the field as fast as possible. This is the exam's go-to 'first ambulance' name-and-date pairing.
points.zh: 1790年代：军医 Jean Larrey 创立 ambulances volantes——『飞行救护车』，把救治尽快送到战场伤员身边。这是考试最爱出的『第一辆救护车』人名—年代配对题。

points.en: The wars drove the leaps: World Wars I and II evolved battlefield corps for field treatment and transport; in the 1950s Korean War, military researchers realized pushing hospital-type services toward the front improved survival — helicopters flew casualties to MASH units (Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals), saving thousands.
points.zh: 每次飞跃都由战争推动：一战、二战不断改进战地救治与后送体系；1950年代朝鲜战争中，军方研究者发现把『医院级』服务前推到战场附近能提高存活率——直升机把伤员送往 MASH（陆军移动外科医院），拯救了数以千计的军人与平民。

points.en: Late 1950s to early 1960s, some European countries swung back to bringing the hospital to the patient with physician-staffed mobile intensive care units (MICUs). North America imported the concept but had too few willing physicians — which forced the founding question of the profession: can a non-physician be trained to perform advanced medical skills? Enough physicians said yes, and the paramedic was born.
points.zh: 1950年代末到1960年代初，一些欧洲国家改走『把医院搬到患者身边』的路线：由受过专门训练的医生驻守移动重症监护单元（MICU）。北美引进了这一概念，却凑不齐愿意出车的医生——由此逼出了这个职业的『创始之问』：非医生能否被训练去执行高级医疗技能？足够多的医生回答『能』，救护员职业就此诞生。

points.en: 1965: the US National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council white paper Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society listed 10 critical points for a functioning EMS system — among them a single nationwide emergency number, automatic caller-location information, EMS legislation in every jurisdiction, resources for medical direction, linked information systems, and a national research agenda. It triggered the National Highway Safety Act of 1966, which created the US Department of Transportation to fund basic and advanced life support programs.
points.zh: 1965年：美国国家科学院/国家研究委员会发表白皮书《意外死亡与残疾：现代社会被忽视的疾病》，列出建立可运转 EMS 系统的10条关键要点——包括全国统一急救电话、来电自动附带定位信息、各辖区通过 EMS 立法、为医疗指导配置资源、贯通全程的信息系统、国家级研究议程等。它直接催生了1966年《国家公路安全法》，据此设立美国交通部（US DOT），为基础与高级生命支持项目提供授权和经费。

points.en: 1969: Dr. Eugene Nagel of Miami trained fire department firefighters in advanced emergency skills and built a telemetry system that let them transmit ECGs to Jackson Memorial Hospital and receive radio orders back — the working prototype of online medical control. He is called the father of paramedicine in the United States. 1971: AAOS published the first US EMT textbook; 1977: the US DOT issued the first National Standard Curriculum for paramedics, built on the work of Dr. Nancy Caroline.
points.zh: 1969年：迈阿密的 Eugene Nagel 医生训练消防员掌握高级急救技能，并搭建了遥测系统——消防员把患者心电图传回 Jackson Memorial 医院，再通过无线电接收医生指令——这正是『在线医疗控制』的雏形。他被称为美国急救医学之父。1971年：AAOS 出版美国第一本 EMT 教科书；1977年：美国交通部颁布第一版急救员国家标准课程，其蓝本是 Nancy Caroline 医生的工作。

points.en: Canadian firsts: Toronto fielded its first organized ambulance service in 1832 — mainly hauling victims of the cholera outbreak sweeping the city then called York; Saskatchewan launched one of Canada's first air ambulance programs in 1946, inspired by the UK's Royal Flying Doctor successes; British Columbia created an organized ambulance service in 1974 on government recommendations.
points.zh: 加拿大的『第一次』：多伦多1832年出现第一支有组织的救护车队——主要转运当时席卷这座还叫『约克』的城市的霍乱患者；萨斯喀彻温省1946年开办加拿大最早的空中救护项目之一，灵感来自英国皇家飞行医生计划的成功；不列颠哥伦比亚省1974年依政府建议建立起有组织的救护车服务。

points.en: The Canada Health Act (1984) funds health insurance publicly on five principles — public administration, accessibility, comprehensiveness, universality, portability. The exam trap: paramedic and ambulance services are not hospital-based, so they fall outside the Act's funding; each province and territory funds EMS its own way, delivering services with accountability to the federal government.
points.zh: 《加拿大卫生法》（1984）以公共资金支付医保，立于五项原则——公共管理、可及性、全面性、普遍性、可携性。考试陷阱在这里：救护车和急救服务不属于医院服务，因此不在该法的资助范围内；各省与地区各自决定 EMS 的筹资方式，服务由省级承担、对联邦负责。

points.en: Canadian professional infrastructure, in exam-ready pairs: Paramedic Association of Canada (PAC, formerly the Canadian Society of Ambulance Personnel) formed 1984, now representing over 20,000 practitioners including the Canadian Armed Forces; paramedic training entered the Canadian Medical Association's accreditation process in the early 1990s, a role now held by Accreditation Canada; Paramedic Chiefs of Canada incorporated 2002 as the national leadership forum.
points.zh: 加拿大的行业组织，按『名称—年份』配对记：加拿大救护员协会（PAC，前身为加拿大救护人员学会）1984年成立，现代表超过2万名从业者，包括加拿大武装部队的救护人员；1990年代初，救护员培训项目纳入加拿大医学会的认证体系，如今这一职责由 Accreditation Canada 承担；加拿大救护长官联合会（PCC）2002年注册成立，是全国性的领导层论坛。

points.en: The NOCP timeline you must keep straight: PAC issued the first National Occupational Competency Profiles in 2001 — the first document defining the core competencies required to practise in Canada; the review began at a 2006 future-vision conference; and in 2011 the Canadian Organization of Paramedic Regulators and PAC agreed to adopt the 2011 NOCP as the foundation for a national paramedic examination.
points.zh: 必须理顺的 NOCP 时间线：PAC 于2001年发布第一版《国家职业能力档案》（NOCP）——加拿大第一份界定执业核心能力的文件；修订工作始于2006年的未来愿景会议；2011年，加拿大救护监管者组织（COPR）与 PAC 达成协议，采纳2011版 NOCP 作为全国救护员统一考试的基石文件。

points.en: The PCC's 2007 white paper The Future of EMS in Canada: Defining the New Road Ahead set six strategic directions: clear core identity, stable funding, systematic improvement (EMS must prove its quality regularly and transparently, not just claim it), personnel development, leadership support, and mobilized health care — paramedics delivering definitive primary care beyond traditional clinical venues.
points.zh: PCC 2007年白皮书《加拿大 EMS 的未来：定义新的前路》定下六大战略方向：清晰的核心身份、稳定的经费、系统性改进（EMS 必须定期、透明地『证明』自己做得好，而不是嘴上说说）、人员发展、领导力支撑、机动化医疗——让救护员在传统临床场所之外提供确定性初级照护。

points.en: The chapter's own controversy box: many communities initially fought against 'ambulance drivers playing doctor' — yet today even the smallest communities expect access to ALS-trained personnel. Useful as the one-line story of the profession's acceptance curve.
points.zh: 本章自带的『争议框』：许多社区起初强烈反对『救护车司机扮医生』——而今天，连最小的社区都理所当然地要求配备受过 ALS 训练的人员。这句话就是这个职业被社会接纳曲线的一行版。

sections.titleEn: The Paramedic System: From Caller to Critical Care
sections.titleZh: 救护系统：从报警人到重症转运

points.en: The system's first link is the citizen, not the ambulance: the public must be taught three things — how to recognize that an emergency exists, how to activate EMS, and how to give basic care before paramedics arrive. Expect the public's definition of 'emergency' to differ dramatically from yours: a 0200 call for a 'sick person' may be a common cold and a sleepless night. You are a public servant; nonemergent calls are part of the job, and the general symptoms they present can still hide a serious problem.
points.zh: 系统的第一环是市民，不是救护车：必须教会公众三件事——识别紧急情况的存在、启动 EMS 系统、在救护员到达前实施基础救护。还要有心理准备：公众对『紧急』的定义可能与你天差地别——凌晨两点的『有人病了』，到场可能只是感冒睡不着。你是公共服务者，非紧急呼叫本来就是工作的一部分，而且这些笼统的症状背后仍可能藏着重症。

points.en: The dispatcher is the caller's first contact: receives and enters all call information, interprets it, and relays it to the right resources. Training requirements vary greatly province to province. A formally trained emergency medical dispatcher adds prearrival instructions — coaching CPR or bleeding control over the phone before crews arrive. Larger services split the role into call-taking (determining the caller's needs) and dispatching (talking to front-line crews and allocating resources).
points.zh: 调度员是报警人的第一接触点：接收并录入呼叫的全部信息、做出解读、再转给合适的资源。各省对调度员培训的要求差异很大。受过正规训练的『急救医疗调度员』（EMD）多一项任务：电话指导到场前急救——如 CPR、止血。大型机构把调度拆成两个岗位：接警（判断呼叫者需要什么）与派遣（与一线班组通话、调配资源）。

points.en: Dispatch information is a starting hypothesis, not a fact: scene findings do not always match what dispatch relayed, yet you begin building the care plan, transport method, and receiving-facility choice from that information en route — then verify on arrival. Facility choice runs on two questions: does the receiving facility have the resources this patient needs, and if not, is an appropriate facility within reasonable distance?
points.zh: 调度信息是初始假设，不是事实：现场所见未必与调度转述一致，但你在途中就要凭这些信息开始搭建救护计划、选定转运方式和接收医院——到场后再验证修正。选医院靠两问：接收机构有没有这名患者需要的资源？没有的话，合理距离内有没有合适的机构？

points.en: Emergency medical responder (first responder): not every province or territory certifies this level, and requirements vary considerably where it exists. Generically it means a person trained in CPR and/or first aid, often part of a first-response agency such as a fire service — and one of your jobs as a paramedic is to know exactly what the first responders in your own system are trained to do.
points.zh: 急救医疗响应员（EMR，即 first responder）：并非每个省和地区都设这一级认证，设了的地方要求也差异很大。通用含义是受过 CPR 和/或急救培训的人员，常隶属消防等第一响应机构——而救护员的职责之一，就是弄清自己系统里的第一响应者到底受过什么训练。

points.en: Primary care paramedic — the backbone and primary provider level of most Canadian systems, caring for and transporting the full spectrum of patients. PCP scope beyond oxygen, wound care, and splinting: a select list of medications for common symptoms such as ischemic chest pain and shortness of breath; defibrillation of unstable rhythms with manual and automated defibrillators; in some regions supraglottic airways; and in some, initiating or maintaining IV lines with certain fluid therapies.
points.zh: 初级救护员（PCP）——大多数加拿大系统的骨干与主力执业层级，负责全谱系患者的救治与转运。PCP 的执业范围在给氧、伤口处理、夹板固定之外还包括：针对常见症状（如缺血性胸痛、呼吸困难）的少量选定药物；用手动和自动除颤器对不稳定心律除颤；部分地区可用声门上气道；部分地区可建立或维持静脉通路并实施特定输液治疗。

points.en: Advanced care paramedic — delivers what is traditionally called ALS on top of the PCP base: intubation, cricothyrotomy, and needle decompression, plus a medication list spanning cardiac, respiratory, neurologic, and endocrine emergencies. Critical care paramedic — works mainly in air ambulance or land-based critical care interfacility transfer; patients are complex, often on multiple medications, blood products, and mechanical ventilation, and CCPs join hospital teams for transfers on specialized support such as ECMO. The trap: a CCP's primary role is moving critically ill patients between facilities, not scene response.
points.zh: 高级救护员（ACP）——在 PCP 基础上提供传统意义的 ALS：气管插管、环甲膜切开、针刺减压，药物清单覆盖心脏、呼吸、神经、内分泌急症。重症救护员（CCP）——主要从事空中或陆路的院间重症转运；患者病情复杂，常需多种药物、血制品和机械通气，CCP 还与院内团队协作完成 ECMO 等特殊支持下的转运。考点陷阱：CCP 的首要角色是院间转运危重患者，不是现场出勤。

points.en: Every scope of practice is defined by the NOCPs and gets reevaluated over time — scope is a living document, not a lifetime grant. And a systems responsibility that has emerged for all Canadian paramedics: recognizing which patients need designated specialty hospitals — acute myocardial injury, stroke, trauma, pediatric emergencies, and burns — so the transport decision is part of the treatment.
points.zh: 每一级的执业范围都由 NOCP 界定，并会定期重新评估——scope 是活文件，不是终身授权。近年加拿大所有救护员新增的一项系统性职责：识别哪些患者需要送往指定专科医院——急性心肌损伤、卒中、创伤、儿科急症、烧伤——转运去向本身就是治疗的一部分。

points.en: Where the profession is heading, per the book: mobile health care and community-based programs, transport to destinations other than hospitals, treat-and-release for patients who need nothing beyond what the paramedic provides, and deeper integration into regional health systems as a primary- and preventive-care resource. Systems must also handle obstetric, pediatric, and geriatric emergencies — procedures, drug dosages, and assessment techniques all differ across children, adults, and older people.
points.zh: 教材指出的职业走向：机动化医疗与社区项目、把患者送往医院以外的目的地、对无需进一步服务的患者『治疗后就地放行』（treat-and-release），以及更深地融入区域医疗体系、成为初级与预防照护资源。系统还必须应对产科、儿科、老年急症——儿童、成人、老人的操作流程、药物剂量乃至评估手法都不相同。

sections.titleZh: 救护员教育：入门与继续教育

points.en: Initial education is province-shaped but NOCP-based. PCP training happens mostly at community colleges, typically (not always) before being hired, and program length swings hard by province: under 1 year in British Columbia versus over 3 years in some Quebec programs. ACP programs run 1 to 2 years, also at college level, and many entrants are already working PCPs — service-based ACP training is not uncommon.
points.zh: 入门教育各省形态不同，但底层都以 NOCP 为基准。PCP 培训多在社区学院完成，通常（并非总是）在被机构录用之前，学制省际差距悬殊：不列颠哥伦比亚省不到1年，魁北克的一些项目超过3年。ACP 课程为1到2年，同样在学院层级，许多学员入学时已是在职 PCP——由服务机构自办的 ACP 培训并不罕见。

points.en: CCP education is the scarce tier: Canada has very few accredited CCP programs, and they are almost entirely run through air ambulance programs. Across all levels, the yardstick of a program is quality — Accreditation Canada accredits a program once it demonstrates minimum standards based on the NOCPs — and the projected future is university baccalaureate-level paramedic education, matching other allied health professions.
points.zh: CCP 教育是稀缺层：全加拿大受认证的 CCP 项目寥寥无几，且几乎全部由空中救护项目运营。无论哪个层级，衡量项目的标尺是质量——Accreditation Canada 在项目证明达到基于 NOCP 的最低标准后予以认证——而可预见的未来是大学本科层级的救护员教育，向其他专职医疗行业看齐。

points.en: Continuing education is externally audited: most provinces require paramedics to show proof of hours. Its three stated jobs — deliver new research findings and techniques, prevent degradation of skills you rarely use, and surface current provincial issues affecting care quality. Internet-based courses count only if they meet your provincial requirements.
points.zh: 继续教育有外部审计：大多数省要求救护员出示学时证明。它的三项本职——传递新研究与新技术、防止不常用技能生疏退化、揭示影响本省救护质量的当下议题。网络课程只有在符合本省规定时才被承认。

points.en: How to widen the knowledge base, per the book: attend conferences and seminars including ones outside your region or province, and even ones not designed for paramedics; read paramedicine and emergency medicine journals or join a journal club; and get the whole service into postcall reviews — the named tool for finding problem areas in your practice.
points.zh: 教材给出的拓宽知识面清单：参加会议与研讨班，最好有些在本地区、本省之外，甚至不妨去非救护员主题的会议；读急救医学与院前医学期刊，或加入期刊俱乐部；再把全机构拉进出勤后复盘（postcall review）——这是书中点名的发现执业薄弱环节的工具。

points.en: Two accountability one-liners worth quoting on the exam: the number of calls you run is not what decides how much more training you need; and no matter what regulators mandate, responsibility for continuing medical education ultimately rests with you — you are the one who lives with the questions after something goes wrong in the field.
points.zh: 两句值得原样进考场的问责金句：出勤次数的多少，并不决定你还需要多少训练；无论监管者规定了什么，继续医学教育的最终责任在你自己——现场出了差错之后，要带着疑问与自责过日子的人是你。

points.en: The common goal shared by many national organizations is promoting uniformity of EMS standards and practices — that phrase is the answer when an exam asks why joining matters. The Canadian roster to recognize: Paramedic Association of Canada, Paramedic Chiefs of Canada, Society for Prehospital Educators in Canada (SPEC), Canadian Transport Medicine Association (CTMA), Canadian Association of Emergency Physicians (CAEP), and the Heart and Stroke Foundation. Membership also buys resources for developing yourself, your service area, and your problem-solving.
points.zh: 众多全国性组织共同的目标是一句话：推动 EMS 标准与实践的统一——考卷问『为什么要参加行业组织』时，答案就是它。要能认出的加拿大名单：加拿大救护员协会（PAC）、加拿大救护长官联合会（PCC）、加拿大院前教育者学会（SPEC）、加拿大转运医学协会（CTMA）、加拿大急诊医师协会（CAEP）、心脏与卒中基金会。入会还附带发展自己、发展辖区、锤炼解决问题能力的资源。

points.en: Practising paramedic functions before you are registered, licensed, and/or certified is unlawful — the book names the offence: practising medicine without a licence. Which credential you need is set by provincial, regional, or local guidelines, and this chapter treats 'certified' and 'licensed' as interchangeable (the fine distinctions live in Chapter 4).
points.zh: 在完成注册/执照/认证之前就以救护员身份执业是违法的——教材点明罪名：无照行医。你需要哪一种资格由省、区域或地方规范决定；本章行文中『认证』与『持照』视为同义（细致区分放在第4章）。

points.en: Certification proves you finished training and met provincial requirements — it does not authorize independent practice: paramedics work under the supervision of the service's physician medical director, who delegates medical acts. How much is delegated depends on the jurisdiction, the service, and the agreement with the delegating physician.
points.zh: 认证证明的是你完成了培训、达到了省定要求——但它不等于可以独立执业：救护员在所属机构医学总监（医生）的监督下工作，由其授权（delegate）医疗行为。授权的宽窄取决于辖区、机构以及与授权医生的协议。

points.en: Registration is the third word with its own meaning: a recognized board of registration keeps the records of your training, local licensure, and recertification, and being registered implies you passed the required provincial testing. Some provinces additionally demand graduation from an accredited program — and Accreditation Canada is the only national accrediting agency for paramedic training programs in Canada.
points.zh: 『注册』是第三个有独立含义的词：由认可的注册委员会保存你的培训、本地执照与再认证记录，注册在案即意味着你已通过省级规定的考核。部分省份还要求毕业于受认证的项目——而 Accreditation Canada 是加拿大唯一的全国性救护员培训项目认证机构。

points.en: Reciprocity = one province or agency recognizing a paramedic credentialed by another. The spectrum of what it takes: some provinces only ask that you be in good standing where you currently practise; others make you challenge their own written and/or practical evaluations; still others request your training transcript and continuing-education hours. Never assume a credential travels automatically.
points.zh: 互认（reciprocity）＝一个省或机构承认另一省/机构授予的救护员资格。门槛从低到高排开：有的省只要求你在现执业省信誉良好；有的要求你『挑战』其笔试和/或实操考核；还有的要调阅你的培训成绩单和继续教育学时。永远别默认资格能自动跨省通行。

sections.titleEn: Professionalism: Attributes You Can Be Tested On
sections.titleZh: 职业素养：会被逐条考到的品质

points.en: A profession is a field of endeavour demanding a specialized set of knowledge, skills, and expertise, usually acquired through lengthy training. A health care professional carries six listed attributes: conforms to the same standards as other health care professions, provides quality patient care, instills pride in the profession, strives continuously for high standards, earns the respect of peers, and meets society's expectations of the profession on duty and off.
points.zh: 『专业』的定义：需要一整套专门知识、技能与造诣的领域，通常经长期训练才能掌握。『医疗卫生专业人员』则有六条列名特质：与其他医疗行业遵循同等标准、提供高质量患者照护、为职业注入自豪感、持续追求高标准、赢得同行尊重、无论当班与否都符合社会对这一职业的期待。

points.en: People form their first judgment of you within the first 10 seconds of meeting — and you meet new people every day. You represent your agency, city, and province; arriving in dirty clothes, with dirty hands, smelling offensive, is named as unacceptable. Confidence and credibility are clinical tools: without them, patients do not let you deliver your best care. Safety footnote: skip long necklaces, dangling earrings, and other jewellery that can interfere with the work.
points.zh: 人们在与你见面的头10秒内就会形成第一判断——而你这行每天都在见新的人。你代表着所属机构、城市和省份；穿着脏衣服、带着脏手、气味刺鼻地到场，被教材直接点名为不可接受。自信与可信度是临床工具：患者不信你，你的最佳救治就无从施展。安全脚注：别戴长项链、垂坠耳环等可能妨碍操作的饰品。

points.en: Integrity is named the single most important attribute of a paramedic — being open, honest, and truthful with patients. The rest of the attribute list: empathy, self-motivation (internal drive for excellence, performing with minimal supervision), communication (listen well, speak directly, no confusing medical jargon with patients), teamwork and respect, patient advocacy, injury prevention, and careful delivery of service.
points.zh: 正直（integrity）被点名为救护员最重要的一项品质——对患者开放、诚实、不说假话。其余列名品质：同理心；自我驱动（对卓越的内在追求，在最少监督下也能胜任）；沟通（认真倾听、直接表达、对患者不甩晦涩医学术语）；团队协作与尊重；患者代言；伤害预防；审慎执业。

points.en: In the prehospital setting the paramedic is most often the team leader — and the book defines leading negatively as well as positively: a leader does not undermine the team, but guides and supports it, stays flexible and open to change at any moment, and resolves problems with team members at an appropriate time and place, not in front of the scene.
points.zh: 在院前环境中，救护员通常就是团队领导——教材从正反两面定义了『领导』：领导者不拆自己团队的台，而是引导和支持团队，随时保持灵活、接受改变，并在合适的时间与场合和队员解决分歧，而不是当着现场的面。

points.en: Patient advocacy has teeth: act in the patient's best interest while respecting their wishes, beliefs, lifestyle, and culture regardless of your own; never let personal feelings alter care; keep conversations about the patient away from anyone not on your team. And advocacy explicitly includes surveillance — stay alert for spousal abuse, child abuse or neglect, and elder abuse or neglect, and report suspected abuse to the appropriate authorities.
points.zh: 患者代言不是空话：以患者最佳利益行事，同时尊重其意愿、信仰、生活方式与文化——不管你自己怎么看；绝不让个人好恶影响救护；谈论患者的对话要避开团队以外的任何人。代言还明确包含『侦察』义务——警惕配偶虐待、儿童虐待或忽视、老人虐待或忽视，一旦怀疑就向相应主管部门报告。

points.en: Injury prevention is written into professionalism because the paramedic sees what no clinician sees — the patient's surroundings before transport. Spot a hazard like a loose rug at the top of the stairs and raise it diplomatically with patient or family; push bike helmets, safety belts, and child car seats whenever the chance arises. Careful delivery of service closes the list: attention to detail, continuous self-evaluation, treating other medical professionals as resources rather than adversaries, and following policies, protocols, procedures, and superiors' orders.
points.zh: 伤害预防写进职业素养清单，是因为救护员看得到任何院内医生看不到的东西——转运前患者的生活环境。发现楼梯口松动的地毯之类隐患，就用外交手腕向患者或家属提出来；一有机会就宣传自行车头盔、安全带、儿童安全座椅。清单收尾是审慎执业：注重细节、持续自评与复评、把其他医疗专业者当资源而非对手，并遵守政策、protocol、流程和上级指令。

sections.titleEn: Roles and Responsibilities: The Eight-Phase Call
sections.titleZh: 角色与职责：一次出勤的八个阶段

points.en: Every call runs the same eight-phase sequence — preparation, response, scene management, patient assessment and care, management and disposition, transfer of care, documentation, return to service. Ordering questions from this list are cheap marks: documentation comes after transfer of care, and return to service is a responsibility, not a rest.
points.zh: 每次出勤都走同一条八阶段链：备勤 → 响应 → 现场管理 → 患者评估与救治 → 处置与去向决策 → 交接 → 文书 → 恢复待命。这张清单的排序题是白送的分：文书在交接之后，『恢复待命』本身是职责的一环，不是休息。

points.en: Preparation means fit physically, mentally, and emotionally, knowledge and skills current, equipment appropriate and in working order. Response has a named sin: driving at high speed with lights and sirens, without due regard for the safety of yourself, your partner, your patient, and everyone on the road, is not acceptable — even when other drivers should yield and do not.
points.zh: 备勤＝身体、心理、情绪三方面都在状态，知识技能不掉线，装备齐全且完好可用。响应阶段有一条点名的红线：开着警灯警笛高速行驶、却不顾自己、搭档、患者及道路上他人的安全，是不可接受的——哪怕别的司机本该让行却没让。

points.en: Scene management fixes the safety order: yourself first, then your team, then the patient and bystanders. Scene safety preparation starts with PPE — gloves, masks, goggles — and you personally set the safety example for the team. Assessment then runs organized, prioritizing the injuries and illnesses most urgently needing treatment.
points.zh: 现场管理钉死了安全顺位：先自己，再团队，然后才是患者和旁观者。现场安全的准备从个人防护装备开始——手套、口罩、护目镜——而且你本人就是团队的安全示范。评估则要有条理地进行，按『最急需处理的伤病优先』排序。

points.en: Management and disposition is where medical direction becomes practical: follow the protocols the medical director signed off; when the situation falls outside protocol or your scope, contact the medical director or direct medical control for orders — you are the medical director's eyes, ears, and touch. Destination decisions require knowing the capabilities of every receiving facility you might use.
points.zh: 处置与去向阶段是医疗指导落地的地方：按医学总监签署的 protocol 执行；一旦情境超出 protocol 或超出你的执业范围，就联系医学总监或直接医疗控制请求医嘱——你是医学总监的眼睛、耳朵和双手。去向决策的前提，是熟知所有可能接收机构的救治能力。

points.en: The closing phases each carry a legal hook: hand over with a brief, concise report while guarding patient privacy; complete the patient care report immediately after transfer — it is the legal record of your prehospital care, and physicians document, so must you; restock and ready the unit fast, because a unit caught unprepared on the next call can bring nasty legal consequences. The margin note doubles down: documenting equipment repairs and checks is nearly as important as documenting patient care.
points.zh: 收尾各阶段都挂着法律钩子：交接时做简短精炼的汇报，同时保护患者隐私；转交患者后立即完成患者救护报告——它是院前救治的法律记录，医生要写病历，你也一样；快速补充耗材、让车辆恢复出勤状态，因为下一单来时车没备好，可能招来难缠的法律后果。页边注还补了一刀：装备检查与维修的记录，重要性几乎不亚于患者救护记录。

points.en: Beyond the call: educate the public on using EMS appropriately, promote community CPR programs — bystander CPR is named a major determinant of whether a cardiac arrest victim lives or dies — mentor new paramedics, conduct research, and campaign for the system after studying its strengths and weaknesses. Some regions extend paramedic work into community clinics, free-standing emergency facilities, hospitals, and home visits under direct medical control.
points.zh: 出勤之外的角色：教公众正确使用急救服务；推广社区 CPR 项目——旁观者 CPR 被点名为心搏骤停患者生死的主要决定因素之一；带教新救护员；做研究；研究本系统的强弱项后为 EMS 发起有章法的倡导。部分地区的救护员还延伸到社区诊所、独立急诊设施、医院工作，并在直接医疗控制下开展家访。

sections.titleEn: Medical Direction: Online, Offline, and the On-Scene Physician
sections.titleZh: 医疗指导：在线、离线与现场医生

points.en: The acts that separate paramedic levels — procedures, medication administration — are acts normally reserved to physicians and advanced practitioners, delegated to paramedics because legislation rarely grants independent authority. Milestone to remember: the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons recognized prehospital and transport medicine as a formal discipline in 2017, with its own competencies and training requirements for EMS medical leadership in Canada.
points.zh: 区分救护员层级的那些行为——操作、给药——本是医生和高阶执业者的专属，因立法很少赋予救护员独立权限，才以『授权』形式下放。要记的里程碑：加拿大皇家内外科医师学院于2017年将院前与转运医学确认为正式学科，为 EMS 的医学领导层设立了专门的能力标准与培训要求。

points.en: Direct (online) medical control = a physician reachable in real time by radio, telephone, or other electronic means; it delivers immediate, specific patient-care orders, receives telemetry, assesses quality in real time, and can even put help on scene. Indirect (offline) medical control = everything built in advance: protocols, standing orders, procedures, quality improvement, and training. Classify any exam scenario by asking one question — is a clinician deciding this case live, or did a document decide it beforehand?
points.zh: 直接（在线）医疗控制＝能通过无线电、电话或其他电子方式实时联系到的医生；提供即时而具体的救治指令、接收遥测数据、实时评估质量，甚至可派人到场支援。间接（离线）医疗控制＝一切事先建好的东西：protocol、standing order、操作流程、质量改进、培训。判别考题场景只需一问——这个病例是有人在实时拍板，还是文件早就拍好了板？

points.en: The three-document ladder: a protocol is a treatment plan for a specific illness or injury, usually built on national standards (Heart and Stroke Foundation ACLS algorithms serve as the cardiac protocol), and protocols also fix approved equipment and minimum personnel expectations. A standing order is a protocol subtype — a written document signed by the medical director spelling out directions, permissions, and prohibitions for care rendered before contacting direct medical control, defibrillation being the classic example.
points.zh: 三级文件阶梯：protocol 是针对特定伤病的治疗方案，通常依托国家级标准制定（心脏与卒中基金会的 ACLS 流程就是心脏病 protocol 的蓝本），protocol 还规定获批的装备与人员的最低要求。standing order 是 protocol 的一个子类——由医学总监签署的书面文件，写明在联系直接医疗控制之前可以做什么、允许什么、禁止什么，经典例子是除颤。

points.en: A clinical practice guideline sits a step beyond standing orders: recommendation statements aimed at optimal care, deliberately less rigid and prescriptive, relying on the paramedic to select which parts fit this particular patient given condition and environment. The trade-off is explicit — flexibility demands critical thinking and sound decision making; a CPG only works in the hands of a skilled, knowledgeable practitioner.
points.zh: 临床实践指南（CPG）比 standing order 再上一级：以『最优照护』为目标的推荐性陈述，刻意不那么僵硬和指令化，靠救护员结合患者状况与环境因素，自行判断该套用指南的哪些部分。代价写得很明白——灵活性以批判性思维和稳健决策为前提；CPG 只在技能扎实、知识过硬的执业者手里才有效。

points.en: The medical director's job does not end at the hospital door: reviewing patient care reports and driving continuous quality initiatives are part of the role. And the on-scene physician trap: you work with your own medical director and must follow local protocols and standing orders; a bystander physician may take over only by accepting full responsibility for the patient and staying through the entire prehospital phase, riding in the ambulance to the emergency department. Systems should have a protocol for exactly this confrontation — know yours, and keep your cool.
points.zh: 医学总监的工作不止于医院门口：审阅救护报告、推动持续质量改进都是其职责。再看『现场医生』陷阱：你效力于自己的医学总监，必须遵守本地 protocol 与 standing order；旁观医生想接管，只有一个办法——对患者承担全部责任，并全程跟完院前阶段，包括坐上救护车一路陪到急诊科。系统应当为这种对峙情形专门设一条 protocol——熟悉你本地的那条，并且别动气。

sections.titleZh: 系统质量改进：CQI 基础

points.en: Two terms, two tenses: quality assurance evaluates problems that already surfaced and finds solutions; continuous quality improvement assesses current practice and builds ongoing improvement so the problem never arises in the first place. CQI is dynamic, needs a structure in place before assessment starts, and its ultimate focus is improving patient care — ideally with every ambulance call reviewed, feasible or not.
points.zh: 两个术语，两种时态：质量保证（QA）处理的是已经冒头的问题——评估并找解法；持续质量改进（CQI）审视的是当下的做法——通过不断改进，让问题根本没机会发生。CQI 是动态过程，启动评估前系统要先搭好结构，其最终落点是改善患者照护——理想状态下每一次出勤都应复盘，哪怕现实中做不到。

points.en: The CQI loop as the book lists it: identify system-wide problems, review them in depth, evaluate and list remedies, build an action plan, enforce it with time frames, then reexamine the issue. Alongside the fix-loop, three positive outputs: promote the excellence found during evaluation, flag needed modifications to protocols and standing orders, and flag situations the current documents do not address at all.
points.zh: 教材列出的 CQI 环：识别全系统性问题 → 深入审查 → 评估并列出对策 → 制定行动计划 → 带着时限执行 → 回头复查。修复环之外还有三项正向产出：表彰评估中发现的优秀实践；指出 protocol 与 standing order 需要修改之处；标记现行文件完全没覆盖到的情境。

points.en: Peer review rules: it works only with proper, consistent guidelines and an open mind; findings aimed at you are educational tools, since even the best-trained paramedic makes mistakes; in an ideal system reviewers rotate, so you will sit on the panel yourself. Two prohibitions — never use the process to demean a colleague, and never discuss findings with anyone outside the identified review process.
points.zh: 同行评议的规矩：只有在评审者遵循恰当一致的准则、保持开放心态时才有价值；针对你的发现是教学工具——训练再好的救护员也会犯错漏看；理想系统里评审席轮换，你迟早也会坐上去。两条禁令——绝不把评议当贬损同事的工具；绝不与评审流程之外的任何人讨论评议发现。

points.en: Professional accountability closes the chapter: you are responsible for reporting adverse events and near misses to the appropriate authority, both to improve the system and as part of your own remediation cycle. In many provinces paramedics now join error disclosure processes — paramedic, medical director, and support staff meeting patients and families to discuss errors and care concerns face to face.
points.zh: 职业问责为本章收尾：你有责任向相应主管方报告不良事件和险些酿祸的『近失事件』（near miss）——既为改进系统，也作为个人改进与补救循环的一环。许多省份的救护员如今还参与『错误披露』程序——救护员、医学总监与支持人员一起，与患者和家属当面讨论差错与照护问题。

atScene.en: A patient may experience once what you have seen hundreds of times — the anxiety is real to them even when the emergency is not real to you. Treat the 0200 'sick person' with a head cold as a public servant would: no anger at the patient, the career, or the system, and stay alert — vague general symptoms sometimes hide a serious problem.
atScene.zh: 患者一生可能只经历一次你早已见过几百次的场面——即使在你眼里算不上急症，对方的恐慌也是真实的。凌晨两点那个『病人』只是感冒睡不着？以公共服务者的姿态对待：不迁怒患者、不迁怒职业、不迁怒系统，同时保持警觉——含糊的全身症状背后偶尔就藏着重症。

atScene.en: How many calls you have run is not what decides how much more training you need — skill decay tracks what you rarely do, not how busy you are.
atScene.zh: 出勤量的多少不决定你还需要多少训练——技能退化盯上的是你『很少做』的操作，而不是你『忙不忙』。

atScene.en: Jewellery discipline: long necklaces, dangling earrings, and similar items can interfere with the work — leave them off shift.
atScene.zh: 饰品纪律：长项链、垂坠耳环之类会妨碍操作——当班就别戴。

atScene.en: On-scene physician demanding control? Stay polite, state that everything you do must follow your medical director's protocols, and offer the only legitimate handover: the physician takes full responsibility and stays with the patient through the whole prehospital phase, including the ambulance ride to the ED.
atScene.zh: 现场医生要求指挥？保持礼貌，说明你的一切操作必须符合你医学总监的 protocol，然后给出唯一合规的交接选项：这位医生对患者承担全部责任，并全程跟到院前阶段结束——包括坐上救护车一路陪到急诊科。

confusions.en: 'Certified means I can practise on my own.' No — certification proves you completed training and met provincial requirements, but paramedic practice runs on medical acts delegated by the service's physician medical director. Practising before you hold the credential at all is practising medicine without a licence.
confusions.zh: 『拿到认证＝可以独立执业。』——错。认证只证明你完成了培训、达到了省定要求；救护员的执业建立在机构医学总监授权的医疗行为之上。而在取得任何资格之前就动手，性质是无照行医。

confusions.en: Standing orders confuse students on timing: they are the care you deliver BEFORE contacting direct medical control — a signed document of directions, permissions, and prohibitions (defibrillation is the textbook example) — not orders you phone in for. If a live clinician is deciding, that is direct (online) control; if a pre-written document decides, that is indirect (offline) control.
confusions.zh: standing order 最容易在『时间点』上栽跟头：它是你在联系直接医疗控制**之前**就照做的救护——一份签署好的、写明指示/许可/禁止的文件（除颤是标准例子）——不是打电话要来的医嘱。有活人实时拍板＝直接（在线）控制；预先写好的文件拍板＝间接（离线）控制。

confusions.en: 'The Canada Health Act funds ambulance services.' It does not: paramedic and ambulance services are not hospital-based, so they sit outside the Act's public funding — each province and territory funds EMS its own way. The Act's five principles govern health insurance, not your ambulance budget.
confusions.zh: 『救护车服务由《加拿大卫生法》出钱。』——不是：救护与急救服务不属于医院服务，不在该法的公共资助范围内——各省与地区各自决定 EMS 经费。那五项原则管的是医保，不是你的救护车预算。

confusions.en: 'A critical care paramedic is the highest-level scene responder.' The CCP's primary role is interfacility transfer of critically ill patients by air or land — scene response happens, but it is not the job's centre. Conversely, do not downgrade the PCP: in most Canadian regions the PCP is the backbone and primary provider level of the system.
confusions.zh: 『CCP 是现场救援的最高配置。』——CCP 的首要角色是空中或陆路的院间危重患者转运——虽也参与现场出勤，但那不是这份工作的重心。反过来也别看轻 PCP：在加拿大多数地区，PCP 才是系统的骨干与主力执业层级。

confusions.en: Quality assurance versus CQI: QA reacts — it evaluates problems that already exist and finds solutions; CQI prevents — it assesses current practice and builds ongoing improvement so the problem never happens. An answer that has CQI 'finding and fixing problems' has quietly described QA.
confusions.zh: QA 与 CQI 之辨：QA 是反应式的——评估已经存在的问题并寻找解法；CQI 是预防式的——审视当下做法、持续改进，让问题根本不发生。若答案把 CQI 写成『发现问题并修复』，那其实悄悄描述的是 QA。

confusions.en: 'Every province has an EMR certification.' Not all provinces and territories certify the emergency medical responder level, and where it exists the requirements vary considerably — which is exactly why a paramedic must learn what the first responders in their own system are actually trained to do.
confusions.zh: 『每个省都有 EMR 认证。』——并非所有省和地区都设 EMR 这一级认证，设了的地方要求也差异巨大——这正是救护员必须弄清本系统第一响应者实际受训水平的原因。

mnemonics.name: 出勤八连环
mnemonics.en: Prepare, Respond, Secure (scene), Assess, Manage, Transfer, Document, Restock — the eight phases of every call, in order.
mnemonics.zh: 备勤 → 响应 → 控场 → 评估 → 处置 → 交接 → 文书 → 归位——每次出勤的八个阶段，顺序不换。谐音串：『备响场评，处交书归』。

mnemonics.name: CUPPA 一杯茶
mnemonics.en: Canada Health Act principles: Comprehensiveness, Universality, Portability, Public administration, Accessibility — CUPPA, like a cup of tea. Then remember the twist: the Act's cup never pours for ambulances.
mnemonics.zh: 《加拿大卫生法》五原则：全面性（C）、普遍性（U）、可携性（P）、公共管理（P）、可及性（A）——拼成 CUPPA，一杯茶。再记住反转：这杯茶从不给救护车倒。

mnemonics.name: 文件硬度阶梯
mnemonics.en: Protocol → Standing order → CPG runs rigid to flexible: the protocol plans a disease, the standing order pre-authorizes acts before online contact, the CPG hands judgment back to a skilled paramedic.
mnemonics.zh: Protocol → standing order → CPG，从硬到软：protocol 为一种伤病定方案，standing order 预先授权『联系在线控制前』的动作，CPG 把裁量权交还给有真本事的救护员。

mnemonics.name: 1984 双响
mnemonics.en: 1984 fired twice in Canadian EMS history: the Canada Health Act passed, and the Paramedic Association of Canada was formed.
mnemonics.zh: 1984 年在加拿大 EMS 史上响了两枪：《加拿大卫生法》通过，加拿大救护员协会（PAC）成立。同年份捆绑记忆。

selfCheck.qEn: List the eight phases of an emergency call in order. Which phase carries the warning about 'nasty legal consequences'?
selfCheck.qZh: 按顺序说出一次出勤的八个阶段。哪个阶段挂着『难缠法律后果』的警告？
selfCheck.aEn: Preparation, response, scene management, patient assessment and care, management and disposition, transfer of care, documentation, return to service. The legal warning sits on return to service: an unrestocked unit caught by the next call can bring legal consequences.
selfCheck.aZh: 备勤、响应、现场管理、患者评估与救治、处置与去向、交接、文书、恢复待命。法律警告挂在『恢复待命』上：下一单来了车却没补齐装备，可能招来法律后果。

selfCheck.qEn: Direct versus indirect medical control — sort these into the right bucket: telemetry review of a live ECG, a signed defibrillation standing order, protocol development, an on-air order to give a medication, training programs.
selfCheck.qZh: 直接 vs 间接医疗控制——把下列各项归入正确一侧：实时读回传心电图、签署好的除颤 standing order、制定 protocol、电台里下达的给药医嘱、培训项目。
selfCheck.aEn: Direct (online): live telemetry, on-air medication orders — plus real-time quality assessment and on-scene assistance. Indirect (offline): standing orders, protocol development, procedures, quality improvement, training.
selfCheck.aZh: 直接（在线）：实时遥测、电台给药医嘱——还包括实时质量评估与到场支援。间接（离线）：standing order、protocol 制定、操作流程、质量改进、培训。

selfCheck.qEn: Give the NOCP timeline: who issued it, when, and what happened in 2011?
selfCheck.qZh: 说出 NOCP 的时间线：谁发布、何时发布、2011 年发生了什么？
selfCheck.aEn: The Paramedic Association of Canada issued the first National Occupational Competency Profiles in 2001 — the first document defining core competencies for Canadian practice. After a review begun at a 2006 conference, the Canadian Organization of Paramedic Regulators and PAC agreed in 2011 to adopt the 2011 NOCP as the foundation of a national paramedic examination.
selfCheck.aZh: 加拿大救护员协会（PAC）2001 年发布首版《国家职业能力档案》——加拿大第一份界定执业核心能力的文件。修订自 2006 年愿景会议启动，2011 年加拿大救护监管者组织（COPR）与 PAC 达成协议，采纳 2011 版 NOCP 作为全国救护员考试的基石。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the Canada Health Act's five principles, and state the funding fact about ambulance services the exam loves.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出《加拿大卫生法》五项原则，并说出考试最爱考的那条救护车经费事实。
selfCheck.aEn: Public administration, accessibility, comprehensiveness, universality, portability. Paramedic and ambulance services are not hospital-based, so they are excluded from the Act's funding — provinces and territories each fund EMS their own way.
selfCheck.aZh: 公共管理、可及性、全面性、普遍性、可携性。救护与急救服务不属于医院服务，因此不在该法资助范围内——各省与地区自行决定 EMS 经费。

selfCheck.qEn: Who is called the father of paramedicine in the United States, and what two things did he do in 1969?
selfCheck.qZh: 谁被称为美国急救医学之父？他在 1969 年做了哪两件事？
selfCheck.aEn: Dr. Eugene Nagel of Miami: he trained Miami Fire Department firefighters in advanced emergency skills, and built a telemetry system letting them transmit ECGs to Jackson Memorial Hospital and receive radio instructions back — the prototype of online medical control.
selfCheck.aZh: 迈阿密的 Eugene Nagel 医生：其一，训练迈阿密消防局的消防员掌握高级急救技能；其二，搭建遥测系统，让消防员把心电图传回 Jackson Memorial 医院并经无线电接收医生指令——在线医疗控制的雏形。

selfCheck.qEn: A PCP, an ACP, and a CCP each claim cricothyrotomy is in their scope. Who is right, and what marks each level's territory?
selfCheck.qZh: PCP、ACP、CCP 都说环甲膜切开在自己执业范围内，谁说得对？三个层级各自的地盘怎么划？
selfCheck.aEn: The ACP: cricothyrotomy, intubation, and needle decompression are ACP-level acts, with medications spanning cardiac, respiratory, neurologic, and endocrine emergencies. The PCP holds the backbone role — select symptom-relief medications, manual and automated defibrillation, sometimes supraglottic airways and IVs. The CCP's territory is critical care interfacility transfer: complex patients on multiple medications, blood products, mechanical ventilation, up to ECMO transfers.
selfCheck.aZh: ACP 说得对：环甲膜切开、气管插管、针刺减压属 ACP 层级，药物覆盖心脏、呼吸、神经、内分泌急症。PCP 是骨干层——少量对症药物、手动与自动除颤，部分地区可用声门上气道和静脉通路。CCP 的地盘是院间重症转运：多药并用、血制品、机械通气的复杂患者，直至 ECMO 转运。

selfCheck.qEn: What is reciprocity, and what three different demands might a province make before granting it?
selfCheck.qZh: 什么是互认（reciprocity）？授予互认前，一个省可能提出哪三种不同要求？
selfCheck.aEn: Recognition of a paramedic credentialed in another province or agency. A province may simply require good standing in your current province; may require you to challenge its own written and/or practical evaluations; or may request your training program transcript and continuing-education hours.
selfCheck.aZh: 对另一省或机构授予的救护员资格予以承认。省方可能只要求你在现执业省信誉良好；可能要求你挑战其笔试和/或实操考核；也可能调阅你的培训成绩单与继续教育学时。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Which written exam you will actually sit
bcAlerts.topicZh: 你实际要考的笔试是哪张卷
bcAlerts.bookEn: The chapter ends the NOCP story in 2011: COPR and PAC adopt the 2011 NOCP as the foundation for a national paramedic examination.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材把 NOCP 的故事讲到 2011 年为止：COPR 与 PAC 采纳 2011 版 NOCP 作为全国救护员考试的基础。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Two updates matter for BC candidates. First, the split: the PCP written exam is COPR's national exam, but the EMR written exam is EMALB's own online exam — not COPR. Second, the framework moved on: COPR examinations are now built on the CPCF (Canadian Paramedic Competency Framework), with NOCP-based sittings retired from November 2026.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 对 BC 考生有两处更新。第一，双轨分流：PCP 笔试是 COPR 全国统考，而 EMR 笔试是 EMALB 自设的在线考试——与 COPR 无关。第二，框架已迭代：COPR 考试现基于 CPCF（加拿大救护员能力框架）命题，基于 NOCP 的场次自 2026 年 11 月起停办。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 『执照』在 BC 的具体形态
bcAlerts.bookEn: The book keeps licensure, certification, and registration generic: provincial, regional, or local guidelines determine your status.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材对执照/认证/注册只做通用描述：具体形态由省、区域或地方规范决定。
bcAlerts.bcEn: In BC the credential is an Emergency Medical Assistant (EMA) licence issued by the EMA Licensing Board (EMALB) under the Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation — the Regulation itself appears on the provincial examination reference list. The provincial service the chapter dates to 1974 operates today as BC Emergency Health Services (BCEHS), a single province-wide system.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 在 BC，这份资格是由 EMA 执照委员会（EMALB）依据《Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation》签发的紧急医疗助理（EMA）执照——该规例本身就列在省考参考文献清单里。教材写到的 1974 年建立的全省服务，今天以 BC 紧急健康服务局（BCEHS）的形态运营，是全省单一系统。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Provincial Examination Guidelines p.18–19（Current to June 15, 2026）

bcAlerts.topicEn: Whose protocols count on the practical exam
bcAlerts.bookEn: The book teaches that you follow the protocols and standing orders signed by your own service's medical director, built on national standards such as the Heart and Stroke Foundation algorithms.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材教的是：遵循本机构医学总监签署的 protocol 与 standing order，其蓝本是心脏与卒中基金会流程等国家级标准。
bcAlerts.bcEn: On the BC provincial practical examination there is exactly one clinical standard: EMALB's official examination guidelines. The grading criteria explicitly bar examiners from crediting other agencies' standards — including BCEHS practice and this textbook. Study the employer's protocols for the job; study EMALB's for the exam.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 在 BC 省实操考试里，临床标准只有一个：EMALB 官方考纲。评分标准明文禁止考官采纳其他机构的标准——包括 BCEHS 的实务和这本教材。上岗学雇主的 protocol，赶考学 EMALB 的考纲，两码事。
